title: Public Displays of Capital Injection
summary:
Public Displays of Capital Injection
When the market gets tough, the tough get going. There is no doubt that the public markets provide a tremendous resource for companies trying to raise capital, expand or execute a succession plan. Periods of positive momentum in the business cycle can sometimes supplant the immediate value that would be realized by a company simply due to a warm embrace by the public.

children.title: PTI
children.summary: S&P 500 The PTFI is representative of the earnings on a basket of benchmark tanker trades weighted to each asset class, and in 2011 has averaged 70% percent lower than historical levels over the past ten years. The compounding of poor shipping asset performance with overall weakness in public market sentiment highlights the potential for cash flow difficulties endemic to the industry.

children.title: Staying the Course
children.summary: Equity prices are often derived from expectations for cash flows to be generated by a company's assets, discounted to a present value. On that basis, the short‐sighted nature of the public investor is truly revealed.

children.title: Second Hand
children.summary: Second Hand Sales Newbuild Any continued erosion of asset prices compounded with cash flow strain will likely result in consolidation. But, as contagious as the pervasive bearishness on Wall Street may be, it could only be telling one side of the story.
